newsitem.title: FRANCE: Govt drops Eramet status change - paper.
newsitem.headline: Govt drops Eramet status change - paper.

text.p: The French government has dropped plans to change the legal status of French nickel producer Eramet, the newspaper Les Echos said on Friday.
Company and government officials could not immediately be reached for comment.

In October Eramet's board agreed to review a proposal put forward by majority shareholder, the state-controlled ERAP holding, to change the legal status of Eramet but did not say how long the review would take.
The proposal involved turning Eramet into a company with supervisory and management boards.
But investors had been concerned that a change in the company's legal status might herald the ouster of chairman Yves Rambaud, who opposed plans to curb Eramet's expansion in New Caledonia.
Eramet shares plunged in October on concern over Rambaud's possible ouster and worries the French state may force Eramet to sell some of its mining assets in New Caledonia for political reasons.
A compromise was eventually reached and Eramet's board agreed in principle to a government proposal to reallocate mining reserves in New Caledonia.
But Eramet is now involved in a dispute with the state over the cost of electricity supplies in New Caledonia, Les Echos said.
The government could still seek to replace Rambaud at the next annual shareholders meeting in June, it said.
